subject: Information Theory
title: Fixed vs Variable Length
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Fixed vs Variable Length.

hook.text: ASCII uses exactly 7 bits per character. Simple but wasteful—'E' uses the same space as 'Z'.

buildup.text: Fixed-length codes are easy to parse. Variable-length codes can be shorter on average.

discovery.text: Variable-length codes match codeword length to symbol probability. Frequent symbols get shorter codes.

twist.text: The tradeoff: variable-length codes need careful design to remain unambiguous (prefix-free or delimited).

climax.text: Shannon proved the ideal average code length equals the source entropy. Variable codes approach this limit.

punchline.text: Variable length saves bits. Fixed length saves headaches.

quiz.question: What is the advantage of variable-length codes?
